llm.summary: This is a markdown-only guide for writing Claude hooks, with some risky examples users should harden before copying.

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities match the stated purpose: teaching hook validation, enforcement, logging, context injection, HTTP hooks, and SDK callbacks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Some examples cover high-impact hook behaviors such as raw audit logging, external HTTP callbacks, context injection, and auto-approval; they are presented as examples, not hidden runtime behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains only Markdown files, no executable scripts, no frontmatter hooks, and static/VirusTotal telemetry is clean.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Global and plugin hook examples can affect broad Claude sessions if copied into real settings, but this broadness is described as part of hook scope selection.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Examples write audit, metrics, and state files under ~/.claude; this is purpose-aligned for observability but should be minimized and permissioned in real use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Reasonable to install as a reference guide. Before copying examples into active hooks, avoid raw prompt/tool-input logging, use HTTPS and trusted endpoints for HTTP hooks, require consent before injecting project files into prompts, and do not auto-approve sensitive actions without narrow allowlists and review.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: Context injection and project-context loading are expected topics for a hook-authoring guide; the examples should add consent, preview, and redaction before real deployment.
[SQP-2] expected: HTTP hooks, logging hooks, and cleanup-command examples are relevant to the guide, but several copy-paste snippets need stronger warnings around sensitive payloads, HTTPS, and destructive commands.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Logging full CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT is not a good security-first default, though it appears only as illustrative documentation and not installed behavior.
[E1] expected: Fetching remote configuration is a plausible performance example, but the plain HTTP example should be treated as unsafe placeholder code.
[EA2] expected: PermissionRequest auto-approve/deny is a real hook capability, but users should avoid auto-approval for privileged or destructive actions unless tightly allowlisted.
[RA2] expected: Persistent hook state is a legitimate pattern, but real implementations should document retention, store only minimal metadata, and restrict file access.
